summary:
ACCEPT. Preserves the fleet-toolkit macOS compatibility work as a reviewable artifact package -- the toolkit lives outside the repo at ~/.claude/mai-tai-fleet, so this is the correct shape: the patch, its checksums, the applied-patch log, and a report, committed for review rather than applied silently. RE-HEAD VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: tree a7bb3c811ed0a2e7aac024080dcc9d301010a213 and patch-id 05475a59ffb31c897bc9b8ba97417a64edf25c3d both recomputed by me and matching; base is the current main tip and an ancestor of the head; 5 of 5 agent markers. ⭐⭐ THE PLATFORM COUNTS ARE REPORTED SEPARATELY, WHICH IS WHAT I REQUIRED AND WHAT A COMBINED NUMBER WOULD HAVE HIDDEN: macOS untouched with a system-only PATH 69 passed / 33 failed (the original reproduction); macOS corrected isolated tree 130/0; macOS fresh application of the corrected patch 130/0 (independent run, exact tree match); Windows Git Bash prior head 125/0; Windows Git Bash corrected exact patch 126/0. The four extra macOS passes are Darwin-specific BSD/GNU path controls. ⭐ THE TEST ENVIRONMENT IS HONEST: PATH was /tmp/...:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin with NO /opt/homebrew, so no GNU coreutils masked a BSD defect. That was an explicit requirement and it is met by construction rather than by assertion. ⭐⭐ CODEX DISCLOSED THEIR OWN FALSE GREEN RATHER THAN QUIETLY FIXING IT: the Windows prior head at 125/0 was a REAL count, but a trailing-newline mutation REMAINED FALSE GREEN against it. Reporting a surviving mutant on a superseded head is the behaviour that makes a report trustworthy, and the corrected patch adds the killing test (125 -> 126). ⛔⭐⭐ SCOPE EXCEPTION, GRANTED DELIBERATELY AND RECORDED: I had scoped gate SEMANTICS as out of bounds. This patch CHANGES promote.sh's manifest comparison, and it is right to. The prior code normalised both sides through `$(...)` to cure a false MISMATCH -- and that normalisation created a false MATCH: a PR manifest differing by exactly one terminal newline compared EQUAL and AUTHORISED A CLEAR, in the one gate whose entire purpose is completeness. That is the same trailing-newline hole as the disclosed false green. THE FIX AVOIDS BOTH FAILURE MODES, which is the reason I am accepting it: both sides are now written to FILES and hashed from disk, so neither passes through command substitution and nothing is stripped on either side. Identical content still compares equal; a one-byte difference no longer compares equal. The selftest pins BOTH directions explicitly -- 'a one-byte non-newline manifest difference is REFUSED and clears nothing' and, after `printf '
' >> .pr-manifest`, 'an extra terminal newline byte is REFUSED and clears nothing'. A one-sided test could not have distinguished this bound. NOT MEASURED, stated plainly: this is an ARTIFACT package, so there is no code in the repo for me to mutate. I verified the re-head identity, the report's internal consistency, the PATH isolation, and read the promote.sh comparison change and its two selftest controls out of the patch text. I did NOT apply the patch and re-run the suites myself -- the 130/0 macOS and 126/0 Windows figures are taken on codex's report, corroborated only by the committed applied-patch log. I also did not review the remaining ~1,100 patch lines line-by-line; acceptance rests on the separated platform counts, the honest environment, the disclosed false green, and the gate-semantics change being strictly stricter with both directions tested. ⛔ CONSEQUENCE FOR PROCESS, and this is the operational point: once this is applied and independently green on BOTH platforms, the WINDOWS-ONLY CLOSE-OUT CONSTRAINT CAN LIFT. Until then it stands -- promote.sh's byte-for-byte comparison is exactly where a BSD/GNU difference fails silently, and this package is evidence that it did.
